title: Confidence-gated surge mitigation and rollback heuristics for Optimize batch/cache tuner
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: After an opportunistic rollout of the Optimize auto-tuner, a subset of production traffic experienced an unexpected unit-cost increase and P95/P99 latency regressions. Early indicators pointed to a combination of overly aggressive batching policy changes and a cascading KV cache TTL misalignment that caused increased cache churn under bursty traffic. This ticket captures the incident follow-up: a set of confidence-gated mitigation heuristics, a staged apply/rollback strategy, validation harnesses, monitoring improvements, and documentation updates for on-call and SRE teams.

Root cause analysis (high level):
- The auto-tuner proposed a new batching window optimization that increased average batch fill but also raised tail latency for short-lived interactive sessions.
- A separate change adjusted KV cache TTLs for LRU segments; under bursty patterns this led to cache thrashing and disproportionately higher token decode cost.
- The orchestration apply path executed the tuning change globally after a small canary passed on low-traffic slices; the canary did not emulate burst patterns and missed the failure mode.

Proposed mitigation and design goals:
1) Confidence gating: require multi-metric pass across canaries that includes cost delta, p95/p99 latency, error-rate, and synthetic-burst stress tests before expanding rollout.
2) Surge mitigation heuristics: implement dynamic holdback for cohorts showing >X% cost increase or >Y ms p99 regression, with automatic reduction of batching aggressiveness and temporary increase of cache TTL to stabilize hit rates.
3) Safe staged apply: apply changes in exponentially increasing cohorts with enforced minimum observation windows and automated canary failover to previous config on threshold breach.
4) Rollback policy: replace instant global rollback with tiered rollback and backoff (canary -> small cohorts -> full), plus blacklisting of tuners that flip-flop more than twice in a week.
5) Offline validation: add workload-aware synthetic tests into the PR pipeline to emulate short interactive sessions and bursty traffic shapes.
6) Observability: surface a risk score in Console for 'pending auto-tuner apply' and add derived metrics (cost-per-token delta, cache eviction rate, batch size distribution) to the default Optimize dashboard.

Acceptance criteria:
- New heuristic engine can detect and automatically mitigate the two failure modes in staged simulated runs.
- CI synthetic validation runs catch the regression in a repeatable way.
- Console shows 'apply risk score' and on-call runbook steps are updated.
- Automated rollback triggers within observation windows and logs a clear justification event.

Artifacts and links: PRs, dashboards, runbooks, and postmortem references are attached below.

Longer-term opportunities: tune confidence thresholds adaptively per-customer SLAs, enable manual override with annotated justification, and add a model-variant fallback that prioritizes latency buckets for interactive products.
